title: Design catalog spec
description: Code-led design-catalog spec: declares which @Preview composables (by function name) make up a published sticker sheet, their grouping, sections, captions, and per-component variants. Consumed by scripts/design-artifacts/generate-design-catalog.mjs over a `compose-preview bundle pack` render. Each `preview` MUST equal an exact @Preview function name in the rendered module; validate before rendering with `node scripts/design-artifacts/validate-catalog-spec.mjs`.

system.description: Stable slug identifying the system; the delivery branch is design-artifacts/<system> and the preview server serves it at /<system>/.

title.description: Human-readable catalog name shown in the preview server.

library.description: Informational: the design-system libraries this catalog covers.

module.description: Gradle module path whose @Preview functions this spec references (e.g. ":app", "samples:design-catalog-m3"). Used by validate-catalog-spec.mjs to locate the Kotlin sources; the render is driven separately by the workflow.

modes.description: Informational: the theme modes the sticker sheet covers (e.g. ["light", "dark"]).

modePriority.description: Per-axis render priority for the theme modes: which palettes must be baked into the published bundle and which the preview server produces on demand. Keys are mode names from `modes` plus the `*` wildcard; values are "required" (default) or "deferred". e.g. { "light": "required", "*": "deferred" } bakes one sticker per component and leaves the rest to the serve host's theme switcher. Only stickers that NAME a theme can be deferred, so a component always keeps its primary render. Requires a live path (publish-live-bundle or a buildable `source`) — the export refuses to publish deferred coverage a serve host could not re-render.

breakpoints.description: The named breakpoints the sticker sheet documents and uses as image size axes. Each entry names the breakpoint (`size`) and identifies the renders that belong to it by `device` (the @Preview(device = …) id, matched first — a multipreview expansion's own identity) and/or `widthDp` (matched as a fallback, and used by the live-preview lane to score which annotation produced a sticker), so declaring both is the most robust. When omitted, a catalog whose library includes androidx.wear.compose defaults to the standard Wear round devices (smallRound / largeRound / xlRound / smallSquare, by device id and width). An explicit array, including an empty array, overrides that Wear default. A device id no breakpoint names keeps the generic Material width class, which collapses two distinct renders onto one axis — the export warns when it sees one.

device.description: The @Preview(device = …) id this breakpoint names, e.g. "id:wearos_small_round".

referenceKits.description: Informational: published design-kit URLs a component seeds from for the one-off import (the render stays authoritative).

compareWith.description: Optional slug of a sibling system to pair against on the cross-system compare page; components carry `parallel` handles into it.

display.description: Optional presentation hints carried onto catalog.json so the preview server reads them instead of inferring — the stage surface and the hero preview to feature on the index.

surface.description: The stage background this system's stickers are drawn for. `dark` for a dark-first platform (Wear OS), so a light-on-transparent sticker isn't washed out on a white stage. Absent ⇒ light.

hero.description: The representative preview to feature as the system's hero — a componentId (e.g. "Template/TimeText") or a flattened preview id. Absent ⇒ the server picks one (prefer a screen, else a canonical component).

groupOrder.description: Optional display order for the groups, by name (e.g. ["Buttons", "Selection", "Containment", …]). Presentation config, like `display`: when the inventory is annotation-supplied, the annotation-derived order follows source declaration order, which may not match the intended catalog order — this pins it. Groups not named keep their relative order after the named ones. Ignored groups (no such group) are harmless.

groups.description: The component inventory, grouped. Group order is the display order (or `groupOrder`, when set). OPTIONAL: a catalog can instead declare its inventory with `@CatalogComponent` / `@CatalogVariant` annotations next to the `@Preview`s (the design-artifacts export builds the inventory from them, layering any groups declared here on top as an override). Absent ⇒ the inventory is wholly annotation-supplied.

priority.description: Whether this entry must be baked into the published bundle ("required", the default — rendered, joined, and subject to the strict completeness gate) or may be produced on demand by the preview server ("deferred"). NOTE: entry- and variant-level "deferred" is currently RECORDED BUT NOT ACTED ON — the preview server does not yet read catalog.json's `deferred[]`, so honouring it would drop the entry from `serve --catalogs` instead of rendering it on demand. Until compose-ai-tools#2965 lands, such an entry renders and bakes exactly as "required" (the export and the pre-flight both say so), and it imposes no live-path requirement. It is safe to author ahead of the server. For deferral that takes effect today, use the axis form `modePriority`, which keeps every component present with its primary sticker. When entry deferral does activate: it needs a live path (publish-live-bundle or a buildable `source`), and static consumers (images/, figma/*.svg, the Figma import) will carry required entries only — which is why the default stays "required".

name.description: Sub-heading for this group of components.

section.description: Optional top-level TAB the preview server buckets this group under (Themes / Components / Screens / Animations / …). Sits one level above `name`. Absent ⇒ a flat, untabbed catalog.

componentId.description: Stable id for the component/state, e.g. "Button/Filled". Unique across the whole spec.

preview.description: EXACT @Preview function name that renders this component. Must match a discovered @Preview (or multipreview) function in `module`.

caption.description: One-line description shown under the sticker.

capture.description: What this component exports. `static` (the default) expects a `previews/<id>.png` sticker; a spec entry that renders none is a missing render and the strict publish gate refuses the whole system. `none` DECLARES that this preview exports no sticker — an AndroidView-hosted composable, a horologist ScalingLazyColumn screen, or a GIF-only capture — so it is excluded from the candidate join without counting as missing, and the entry stays in the spec as the record that the coverage is sticker-less (if the content is animated, put its group under `section: "Animations"` to keep it out of the component tabs). Use it only when the render genuinely produces no PNG; deleting the entry instead hides the gap.

reference.description: Optional seed-kit handle (Figma node etc.) for the one-off import.

parallel.description: Optional componentId of the counterpart in the `compareWith` sibling system, paired side-by-side on the cross-system compare page.

component.description: Optional Code Connect override: the production composable name the sticker maps to (takes priority over the inferred target when building code-connect.json).

import.description: Optional Code Connect override: the import line for `component`.

source.description: Optional Code Connect override: the source location (path or URL) for `component`.

variants.description: Extra state/content renders folded onto this sticker; each is its own @Preview.

select.description: Pick ONE value of a multipreview's fan-out for this entry, instead of folding every render of `preview` onto it. Lets two entries share a @Preview function and stay separate cards with their own componentId and caption — the alternative being to split the function in the module into per-breakpoint siblings (which also drops the multipreview's other axes, e.g. @WearPreviewFontScales). A selection that matches no render is reported as a missing render, naming the values the function did produce.

size.description: The breakpoint name (from `breakpoints`) this entry renders at, e.g. "largeRound".

variant.description: A secondary render of the parent component, tagged by `state` (pressed/focused/disabled/…), named `props` content axes, or a `theme` (light/dark, for a screen whose two themes are separate @Preview functions), and optionally narrowed to one breakpoint with `select`. Give at least one so it's distinguishable from the default.

preview.description: EXACT @Preview function name for this variant render.

capture.description: As on a component: `none` declares that this variant render exports no static PNG, so it is skipped in the fold without counting as a missing render.

state.description: The interaction/state this variant shows (pressed, keyboard-focus, disabled, off, …).

props.description: Named content axes distinguishing this variant (e.g. { "content": "icon+label" } or { "locale": "de" }).

theme.description: Pairs a separate-function theme render onto this component so it folds into one …__light/…__dark swap card — use when a screen's light and dark renders are two @Preview functions (e.g. FooScreen + FooScreenDark) rather than one multipreview. The dark render must set uiMode = UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES so its pixels are actually dark; this tag makes the pairing authoritative.
